t: #4027 Elevator Requests III — Bitmask DP over Fulfillment Order
o:
## Understanding the problem
An elevator starts at floor `start`; each second it moves one floor or waits. Request `i` (arrival `a_i`, floor `f_i`) is fulfilled the first moment the elevator is at `f_i` at or after `a_i`. Minimize the time when all requests are done.

Example 1: go 0->5 (arrive 5, wait to 6 for arrival), then 5->8, done at 9. Example 2: 5->7 at time 2 (fulfills request 0), 7->3 arrives 6, wait to 7. Example 3: 3->5->1->3 giving 8.

With at most 16 requests, the only question is the visiting order — a permutation problem, so Held-Karp bitmask DP over subsets with the last visited request is the natural fit. Floors up to 1e9 are irrelevant beyond travel times (absolute differences).
k: Only the order of visiting requested floors matters; travel time between consecutive visits is the absolute floor difference.
If the elevator reaches a floor before the request's arrival, it simply waits — so completion time for the next stop is max(current time + travel, arrival).
Held-Karp DP: dp[mask][last] = earliest time all requests in mask are fulfilled with `last` visited last; answer is min over dp[full][last].

a.i: Enumerate subsets in increasing order. For each (mask, last) with a finite value, extend to any unvisited j: new time = max(dp[mask][last] + |f_j - f_last|, a_j). Single-request masks start from the elevator's start floor. O(2^m · m^2) with m <= 16 is about 16M transitions — fast.
s: For each mask and last in mask, relax dp[mask | 1<<j][j] with max(dp[mask][last] + |f_j - f_last|, a_j).
Answer = min over j of dp[full][j].
a.t: O(2^m · m^2) — every (subset, last, next) triple is relaxed once; m <= 16 so ~16M operations.
a.sp: O(2^m · m) for the DP table.

a.i: The same recurrence written backwards: solve(mask, last) = earliest time all of `mask` are done standing at `last`'s floor, computed from smaller subsets. Memoization on (mask, last) yields identical complexity and is often easier to derive live in an interview.
s: Base case: mask = {last} → max(|f_last - start|, a_last).
Otherwise take min over predecessors i in mask\{last} of max(a_last, solve(mask ^ {last}, i) + |f_last - f_i|).
Answer = min over last of solve(full, last).
a.t: O(2^m · m^2) — each (mask, last) state is solved once with m predecessor candidates.
a.sp: O(2^m · m) for the memo table plus recursion stack.

w:
## Wrap-up
Bitmask DP is the only viable family here given m <= 16; prefer the bottom-up version to avoid recursion limits, and the top-down version if you derive the recurrence on the fly. Pitfalls: forgetting the waiting-for-arrival term (use `max`, not addition), using Manhattan/Euclidean distance instead of absolute floor difference, and integer overflow in languages with 32-bit ints (times reach 1e9 + travel). Follow-ups: capacity limits (elevator carries limited passengers — state must track passengers onboard), or multiple elevators (multiply the state space).
